articles.title: Fever facing offseason questions, uncertain futures for Kelsey Mitchell and Sophie Cunningham after playoff exit: 'We didn't meet that [championship] expectation'
articles.summary: Indiana was bounced by Las Vegas for the second straight postseason.
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever's season came to an end at the hands of the Las Vegas Aces for the second straight season on Friday night.

Despite a fourth consecutive season with an improved record, the Fever have won only a single playoff round since 2016. As the team heads into the offseason, there are several questions that will need to be answered before Kelsey Mitchell, Caitlin Clark and Aliyah Boston and Co. can run it back for the 2027 season.

Mitchell's future is one of those questions. The four-time WNBA All-Star and 2026 scoring champion can become an unrestricted free agent and is unsure about what she will eventually decide.

"It's too early for me to really tell what I need to do," said Mitchell , who has spent her entire nine-year career with the Fever. She added that she has to be "selfish" about making the best decision for her and her family.

"I've obviously built a Fever family here … I guess TBD," Mitchell added while saying, "Heck yeah," when asked if she'd be fine staying with the franchise for the rest of her career.

General manager Amber Cox said Mitchell is a "major priority" in the offseason.

"Our goal is for her to be a Fever girl the rest of her career," Cox said.

Another potential Fever free agent is forward Sophie Cunningham. The 30-year-old finished her second year in Indiana by averaging 7.9 points, 2.3 rebounds and 1.2 assists in 43 games.

Cox said the plan is try to re-sign Cunningham, who inked a one-year deal in April to return.

"Sophie is a really solid leader in the locker room and a great connector ... an important voice in the locker room when we need her. She's an unrestricted free agent, so we'll see where those conversations take us," said Cox, who noted that the off-court controversy involving Cunningham this season will not impact the team's decision to bring her back.

Will head coach Stephanie White could be one of the offseason changes? This was her second season leading the Fever, and Cox said areas that need improvement will be addressed in the offseason.

"I think the expectation is always championship. We didn't meet that expectation, but we're going to learn from it and we're going to grow. Steph's players know that she rides for them," Cox said of White's performance. "She has great relationships with them and just continues to build on that every time we are together. It comes back to that continuity and how you build together."

White expressed an eagerness to stay beyond this season.

"At the end of the day, it's their decision about whether I return or not," White said. "I'd love the opportunity. I love this franchise ... and I hope to continue to be the coach."

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham Calls Out A'ja Wilson For 'Double Standard' in Video, Tells WNBA Star to 'Grow Up'
articles.summary: Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham said she feels the WNBA applied a "double standard" by not disciplining Las Vegas Aces star A'ja Wilson for an incident involving a fan during a first-round matchup between the Aces and Fever.
articles.body:
Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham said she feels the WNBA applied a "double standard" by not disciplining Las Vegas Aces star A'ja Wilson for an incident involving a fan during a first-round matchup between the Aces and Fever.

Cunningham was called for a foul on Wilson in the fourth quarter of the Fever's Game 2 win Tuesday, after which a fan stood and pointed at Wilson .

Wilson, who stepped forward to confront the fan as multiple Aces players ran over to pull her away, did not face any additional discipline past the technical foul she received on the play.

"She's like the LeBron James of our league, and so of course they're not going to suspend her... Something should have happened," Cunningham said on Saturday's episode of her podcast, the No Hesitation Show with Drew Hanlen. "The two people who came off the bench onto the court, that should have happened. I think there's definitely a double standard."

Cunningham added she didn't want Wilson to have been ejected from the game in part because she feels the Fever "would have gotten a lot of backlash from that."

"We yell from the rooftops that we want equality, that we want to be treated like the men, that we want all this stuff and we deserve all these things, and we do, we do deserve it," Cunningham said. "But if you're asking for all these fans to come— and you have new fans, who are real sports fans, and they come and do something that a sports fan would probably do if you're on the opposing team, and then you're going to go for him for just pointing, saying that you fouled? Grow up."

Cunningham also said she felt the Aces benefitted from an "A'ja whistle" after her Fever teammate Caitlin Clark seemingly hinted at criticism of the refereeing of the first-round series by previously reacting to a disparity in foul calls.

Wilson said after Game 2 she saw the fan's actions as "unacceptable" and had apologized to her teammates for taking the tech. She bounced back in Game 3 by scoring 36 points and 10 rebounds as the Aces eliminated the Fever.

She and the Aces have since advanced to the semifinals, where their series against the Golden State Valkyries tips off Sunday at 4 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham says Aces' A'ja Wilson must 'grow up' after confronting fan, who Fever guard believes did nothing wrong
articles.summary: Cunningham said on "No Hesitation" that Wilson's behavior could have been cause for suspension: "But she's like the LeBron James of our league, and, so, of c...
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham, one of the most outspoken members of the Fever, expressed on her podcast with co-host and basketball trainer Drew Hanlen, "No Hesitation," that, "if you want to get technical," Wilson's behavior "could have caused for suspension."

"But she's like the LeBron James of our league, and, so, of course they're not going to suspend her," Cunningham said on an episode released Saturday , two days after Indiana lost a winner-take-all Game 3 to Wilson's Aces .

Cunningham emphasized in that podcast appearance that Wilson — a 30-year-old four-time WNBA MVP and three-time WNBA champion — must "grow up."

Midway through the fourth quarter of Game 2, which the Fever won 99-89 at home on Tuesday, Wilson tried to fight through a screen set by Cunningham. They got tangled up, and Cunningham hit the deck.

Cunningham was called for a foul, much to the dismay of Fever fans, including one sitting behind the basket at Indianapolis' Gainbridge Fieldhouse who pointed at Wilson. That motion, along with what the fan said, angered Wilson.

She intensely approached the fan and said her piece before she was pulled back by teammates and an official.

Wilson was assessed a technical foul for unsportsmanlike conduct, but she remained in the game and ultimately wasn't fined or suspended by the W.

Although the fan was temporarily removed from his seat, he later was allowed to return. The Fever said in a statement after the game the fan didn't violate their rules and the organization wouldn't be investigating the matter further.

Wilson lamented her tech postgame, but she didn't regret her actions.

"If I see a man come at me, taking steps toward me and pointing at me, I don't give a damn what you said. I don't give a damn how you said it, the tone, that is unacceptable," Wilson said after the game . "You don't know me to step towards me and point at me. I'm not for that s*** at all. … That there is unacceptable. How he gets back in the game because they said he didn't do anything, of course he did. "It's just certain things that I'm not going to allow anymore, because it's just unacceptable. You don't know me at all to come and step towards me and point at me and say anything."

I don't give a damn how you said it, the tone, that is unacceptable," Wilson said after the game . "You don't know me to step towards me and point at me. I'm not for that s*** at all. … That there is unacceptable. How he gets back in the game because they said he didn't do anything, of course he did.

articles.title: La ley del ex impera en la victoria de La Laguna Tenerife ante el Unicaja de Txus Vidorreta
articles.standfirst: Marcelinho y Guy acaban con el conjunto malagueño en el reencuentro del técnico con su antiguo equipo
articles.summary: Marcelinho y Guy acaban con el conjunto malagueño en el reencuentro del técnico con su antiguo equipo
articles.body: El Unicaja y Vidorreta fueron víctimas de la ley del ex. La Laguna Tenerife fue mejor que los malagueños en el Martín Carpena para ganar un partido que se decidió al inicio del último cuarto (75-80), cuando el equipo insular encadenó un parcial de 0-10. Kendrick Perry fue el encargado de liderar el inicio ofensivo del Unicaja, mientras que La Laguna Tenerife encontró en el lanzamiento exterior una de sus principales vías de anotación. Los malagueños consiguieron mantener la iniciativa durante buena parte del primer periodo, aunque el conjunto visitante respondió cada vez que el Unicaja intentaba abrir diferencias. Una suspensión de Perry sobre la bocina permitió a los locales terminar por delante el primer cuarto (23-21). La igualdad se mantuvo durante el segundo periodo. La Laguna Tenerife tomó inicialmente la iniciativa, pero el Unicaja fue capaz de reaccionar gracias al acierto de Hunt y a la aportación de sus jugadores exteriores. Ambos equipos intercambiaron ventajas durante varios minutos en un partido con alternativas constantes. Pantzar y Noua volvieron a dar ventaja al conjunto malagueño, aunque el equipo visitante volvió a equilibrar el encuentro antes del descanso. Huertas, con una suspensión sobre la bocina, estableció el empate al término de la primera mitad (39-39). El Unicaja salió mejor tras el descanso y encontró en Brazdeikis una de sus principales referencias ofensivas. La Laguna Tenerife reaccionó rápidamente con Guy y Huertas al frente y volvió a tomar el control del partido. El encuentro continuó con alternativas y sin que ninguno de los dos equipos lograra establecer una diferencia definitiva. El conjunto insular llegó mejor al tramo final del periodo y terminó el tercer cuarto con ventaja (55-59). El inicio del último cuarto resultó determinante. La Laguna Tenerife aprovechó la falta de acierto del Unicaja para encadenar un parcial de 0-10 y abrir una diferencia importante. Los malagueños tardaron casi cuatro minutos y medio en volver a anotar, pero Kravish puso fin a la sequía y Noua contribuyó a reducir la distancia con varias acciones consecutivas. El Unicaja encontró entonces más acierto desde el perímetro y volvió a acercarse en el marcador. Perry asumió protagonismo en los últimos minutos y mantuvo a los locales con opciones de remontada. En el tramo final, el conjunto malagueño llegó a ponerse a una posesión, pero La Laguna Tenerife respondió con un palmeo de Abromaitis y, posteriormente, con dos tiros libres de Jaime Fernández. El Unicaja no pudo completar la remontada y La Laguna Tenerife se llevó la victoria del Martín Carpena por 75-80. 75- Unicaja (23+16+16+20): Perry (23), Hunt (13), Brazdeikis (4), Noua (13), Kravish (9) -quinteto inicial- Barreiro (5), Hernangómez (6), Djedovic (0), Lukosius (0), Pantzar (2), Thomas (0). 80- La Laguna Tenerife (21+18+20+21): Huertas (17), Guy (18), López-Arostegui (6), Abromaitis (7), Happ (8) -quinteto inicial- Fernández (13), Fitipaldo (0), Shermadini (0), Hunter (5), Alderete (0), Doornekamp (3), Kurucs (3). Árbitros: Carlos Peruga, Juan de Dios Oyón y David Sánchez. Incidencias: Partido correspondiente a la jornada 2 de la Liga Endesa, disputado en el Palacio de los Deportes José María Martín Carpena ante 9.936 espectadores. En la previa, el Unicaja homenajeó a su exjugador Omar Cook, actual miembro del cuerpo técnico de los Cleveland Cavaliers de la NBA.

articles.title: What is latest on Marquette's Colin Porter getting a fifth season?
articles.summary: Colin Porter didn't play in Marquette's intrasquad scrimmage because his eligibility with the NCAA remains in limbo.
articles.body:
Marquette men's basketball fans are still waiting to get their first glimpse of Colin Porter.

Who knows if the transfer guard from Liberty will ever appear in a Golden Eagles uniform after suffering a setback in his legal quest for a fifth season of eligibility.

MU coach Shaka Smart held Porter out of the team's intrasquad scrimmage on Oct. 3, a day after the Kentucky Court of Appeals dissolved a temporary injunction in a lawsuit in which Porter and former Menomonee Falls standout Seth Trimble (now at Louisville) are among the plaintiffs.

That lawsuit is still pending. Porter's name is also attached to a similar lawsuit in North Carolina. Players from the class of 2022 recruiting class are seeking fifth seasons because the NCAA has allowed that for the classes that came after 2022.

"Colin is in limbo because of this fifth-year stuff," Smart said. "I guess there's stuff coming up this week with his case.

"So we're just kind of TBD with him, just trying to support him through it. He has been great. I feel bad for him that he's in limbo with this, but he's been awesome with his approach."

This a unique situation for a college basketball coach. It is under a month until MU's first game against Mercyhurst on Nov. 2 at Fiserv Forum.

"Colin is such a great kid," Smart said. "The first thing he said to me is 'I don't want to be a distraction for the team.'

"This was something that we knew when we took him that this could be up in the air, it could be in limbo. We had conversations with people in the NCAA that in this particular case are directly fighting against the fifth-year guys getting eligibility. We decided at that point that it made sense to try to do, but we knew that it wouldn't be 100%.

"Colin knew that as well. He has been phenomenal. Couldn't have been any better in the last five weeks since he's been here. Now our job is to just support the heck out of him. Obviously plan both ways. Prepare both ways, because he's somebody that would definitely make an impact on our team if he can play.

"But if he can't play, then we certainly need to plan for that scenario. Which in all honestly, he wasn't here all summer, so that was something we planning for in the first place."

articles.title: Kelsey Mitchell says she’ll be ‘selfish’ about future as Fever free agency looms
articles.summary: Questions about fan behavior, the Indiana Fever’s future and Kelsey Mitchell’s free agency dominated discussions as members of the Fever met with reporters f...
articles.body:
Questions about fan behavior, the Indiana Fever's future and Kelsey Mitchell's free agency dominated discussions as members of the Fever met with reporters following their playoff elimination.

Mitchell, who has only played in a Fever uniform during her nine WNBA seasons, said she would "be selfish about where my career is going" as an unrestricted free agent. She also discussed the challenges of playing in the spotlight as Caitlin Clark's teammate.

"I don't think people really understand how much we endure, man," said Mitchell, who ranked second in WNBA scoring and set single-game and 3-point records this season. "Like, if I showed y'all my DMs about the hate and all of the stuff that comes with being a professional athlete, but specifically being an Indiana Fever basketball player, it's a lot that goes into that. And those days are hard as hell, man.

"Playing with (Clark) and having the eyes that she's got (on her), we get a lot of flak just from being on her team."

Player-fan tensions have been mounting in the WNBA and were evident during the Fever's first-round playoff series against the Las Vegas Aces. In the Fever's 99-89 Game 2 win at Gainbridge Fieldhouse on Tuesday, reigning MVP A'ja Wilson confronted a fan seated behind the baseline.

Fever general manager Amber Cox defended her team's fans in her exit interview Saturday, saying the "attacks on our fanbase have no basis in reality."

The man who pointed and yelled at Wilson was temporarily removed from his seat but was found to have not violated the fan code of conduct. (Wilson received a technical foul but no further repercussions from the league.) Similarly, in an August game, a fan Jewell Loyd identified to officials was also found to have not broken conduct rules.

"Here's the fact: We did not have one fan pointed out by a player who violated the WNBA code of conduct this season," Cox said. "Not one fan was removed from a game. … Our fans love this team. They're going to cheer, they're going to boo, and sometimes they might point. It's a home-court advantage for a reason, and it's the same for the Pacers. And all of that is within the code of conduct."

Cox said fans who cross the line — in arenas and online — should be held accountable.

Former Indiana forward Brianna Turner, who now plays with the Aces, disputed Cox's characterization of Fever fans.

"This is an unequivocally false statement," said Turner, an eight-year veteran who played 27 games for the Fever in 2025, on X. "Players inside and outside the organization have repeatedly issued complaints with the Fever fanbase. While it's not all Indy fans, it's certainly a trend. To say the attacks have 'no basis in reality' is disingenuous."

The Fever seem eager to keep Mitchell as part of a core with Clark and Aliyah Boston in hopes of becoming title contenders . Mitchell averaged 24.7 points this season and was an MVP contender.

Mitchell told reporters that she's built a "Fever family" in Indiana and that "everything I've grown to be is (because of) the Fever." Free agency begins in late January 2027. Mitchell said she hasn't thought deeply about her options yet so soon after her season ended.

Fever coach Stephanie White lauded her star backcourt's on-court chemistry on Thursday.

"(Mitchell and Clark) complement one another so well," White said. "They make each other better. They make each other's lives easier. They've just been a joy to coach."

articles.title: Trae Young Leaves Door Open for Future Hawks Reunion After Wizards Trade, 'You Never Know'
articles.summary: Even though Trae Young is still in the early stages of a new chapter with the Washington Wizards, he won't close the door on one day potentially returning to his original team.
articles.body:
Even though Trae Young is still in the early stages of a new chapter with the Washington Wizards, he won't close the door on one day potentially returning to his original team.

Appearing on The Baller Alert Show (starts at 12:40 mark), Young said "you never know" when asked if he would at some point consider playing for the Atlanta Hawks again.

"Man, you never know," Young said. "Like that's why the NBA is just such a… For me, I plan on playing for a long time . So, like I that's why I wanted to leave the right way, you know what I'm saying? And for me to not have any like bad blood with anybody in the city or any of the fans. (...) That's that's why I wanted to leave on the right terms. And sometimes breakups are meant to happen, but just how they go down is what's most important. But for me right now, obviously my 10 toes are here in DC. "

Young spent the first eight seasons of his career in Atlanta. He made the All-Star team four times and helped the franchise make three consecutive playoff appearances from 2021 to '23, including a trip to the Eastern Conference Finals in 2021.

After the Hawks didn't sign Young to a contract extension last offseason, it seemed to signal the possibility a split could be coming. The two sides eventually worked together on a trade to find a destination that would benefit him.

Young landed in Washington on Jan. 9 in exchange for CJ McCollum and Corey Kispert. His farewell message to Atlanta fans written on social media did not suggest there were any hard feelings toward the Hawks organization.

Injuries limited Young to just 15 games last season, including five with the Wizards after the deal. Despite his lack of playing time in 2025-26, he secured a four-year, $212 million contract from Washington in free agency.

The Wizards have a fascinating roster going into this season. Young, Anthony Davis, AJ Dybantsa, Alex Sarr and Bub Carrington is an interesting group of five.

Dybantsa's development is the most important thing for Washington, but keeping Young and Davis healthy will go a long way toward determining if this is a playoff team in the East.

Given how popular and important Young was for Atlanta basketball during his time there, it's not a surprise he isn't ruling out a reunion down the line.

For now, though, the Wizards will be hoping to get the best version of Young as they try to take a step forward coming off three consecutive seasons with fewer than 20 wins.

articles.standfirst: El base croata destroza al Kids&Us Manresa con 22 puntos, 10 asistencias y 35 de valoración
articles.summary: El base croata destroza al Kids&Us Manresa con 22 puntos, 10 asistencias y 35 de valoración
articles.body: Un Río Breogán liderado por Dominik Mavra (22 puntos, 10 asistencias y 35 de valoración) y que fue de menos a más, venció con claridad a un Kids&Us Manresa intermitente y desacertado a lo largo de los cuarenta minutos (95-101). A pesar de que los locales realizaron un gran inicio de encuentro y llegaron a mandar por once puntos, el cuadro gallego acumuló progresivamente buenas sensaciones a ambos lados de la pista y se convirtió en una apisonadora, alcanzando los veintidós tantos de diferencia. Además, se ha convertido en el primer equipo en anotar más de cien puntos en las dos primeras jornadas de la liga desde 2004. A la buena actuación de Mavra se sumaron los 17 puntos, 5 rebotes, 5 asistencias y 21 créditos de valoración de Tevin Brown. Por parte del Manresa, Timmy Allen completó una actuación espectacular (30 puntos, 8 rebotes y 35 de valoración), aunque no obtuvo el premio del triunfo para su equipo. Los del Bages, liderados por un gran Rafa Villar (cinco puntos y un tapón en el primer período), iniciaron el partido con una marcha más que los lucenses y lograron situar la primera ventaja de la noche con un parcial de salida 14-3 en apenas dos minutos que obligó al técnico visitante, Luis Casimiro, a pedir el primer tiempo muerto del duelo. Poco a poco, el Breogán se fue encontrando en ataque, pero los locales siguieron intratables de cara al aro y mantuvieron la renta durante varios minutos (21-7, min.5). Sin embargo, un parcial 6-17 de los visitantes en el tramo final del cuarto rebajó la diferencia a tan solo tres tantos (27-24, min.10). En el segundo cuarto, el encuentro entró en una fase de imprecisiones y excesivas pérdidas por parte de ambos conjuntos, una circunstancia que se vio reflejada en la baja anotación durante los primeros cuatro minutos, en los que únicamente se anotó un triple por parte del Manresa y una canasta de dos puntos en el cuadro gallego. Con el paso de los segundos, el conjunto celeste mejoró sus porcentajes y consiguió situarse por delante en el marcador por primera vez en el encuentro, provocando que Diego Ocampo pidiera tiempo muerto hasta en dos ocasiones (34-41, min.17). Los locales no reaccionaron, y ello lo aprovecharon los visitantes, guiados por Dominik Mavra (15 puntos y 8 asistencias en la primera mitad), para aumentar la diferencia antes del paso por vestuarios y completar un parcial 13-27 (40-51, min.20). Tras el descanso, el guión del partido no varió. El Breogán estaba de dulce en ataque y centrado en defensa, y un mate de Tevin Brown estableció una nueva máxima renta para los suyos (46-68, min.24). No obstante, el Kids&Us Manresa no arrojó la toalla. Gracias a una sustancial mejora en los porcentajes desde el perímetro, encadenaron ocho puntos seguidos que obligaron a parar el partido a Casimiro tan solo un minuto más tarde. La ventaja se estabilizó, y el tercer período prosiguió con un largo intercambio de golpes entre ambos equipos en el que ninguno de ellos consiguió romper el marcador. Un arreón final de los visitantes volvió a situar la máxima diferencia tras un triple de Rasir Bolton (67-89, min.30). Al inicio del último cuarto, el conjunto del Bages recibió un nuevo mazazo después de que Nick Ongenda fuera expulsado por cinco faltas personales. No obstante, sin uno de los principales recursos sobre la pista, los de Diego Ocampo fueron capaces de meter algo de miedo a los lucenses (81-94, min.37). Sin embargo, el Río Breogán supo gestionar los instantes finales e impidió que el cuadro local materializara el intento de remontada (95-101). 95 - Kids&Us Manresa (27+13+27+12): Allen (30), Agbo (14), Notae (20), Ongenda (7), Villar (7) -cinco inicial- Kolenda (7), Vila (-), Beaufort (3), Bassas (-), Tamba (6), Enabuele (-) y Minchev (1). 101 - Río Breogán (24+27+38+12): Brown (17), Peris (3), Brankovic (9), Andric (2), Bolton (13) -cinco inicial- Ilic (4), Alonso (13), García (7), Aranitovic (7), Mavra (22) y Kasibabu (4). Árbitros: Fernando Calatrava, Sergio Manuel y Rubén Sánchez Mohedas. Eliminaron a Ongenda y Allen (Kids&Us Manresa) por cinco faltas personales. Incidencias: partido de la segunda jornada de la Liga Endesa disputado en el pabellón Nou Congost de Manresa ante 4.210 espectadores.

articles.title: La mejor noticia en la marejada del Real Madrid
articles.standfirst: Maledon es el base que mejor y más rápido se ha adaptado al baloncesto de Pedro Martínez: líder de los blancos en puntos, asistencias y valoración
articles.summary: Maledon es el base que mejor y más rápido se ha adaptado al baloncesto de Pedro Martínez: líder de los blancos en puntos, asistencias y valoración
articles.body: En el irregular comienzo de temporada del Real Madrid se puede encontrar una buena noticia. Es el rendimiento de Theo Maledon. El francés es el base que antes y mejor ha encajado en la filosofía de baloncesto de Pedro Martínez, bastante por delante de Facundo Campazzo y Andrés Feliz. Tras un primer curso algo gris para lo que se esperaba de él, ha dado un paso adelante en sus prestaciones y en las sensaciones que ofrece en la pista. “Siento que me estoy adaptando más. Estoy empezando a entender mejor el sistema y a encontrar formas de impactar en el juego en ambos lados de la cancha, no sólo en ataque, sino cumpliendo con lo que se requiere en defensa. Para mí está siendo una experiencia de aprendizaje para intentar seguir adelante con esa confianza”, decía antes de la doble jornada de Euroliga de esta semana, donde ha lucido. Maledon se está manteniendo firme en la marejada que vive el Madrid con esas tres derrotas seguidas para comenzar la Euroliga, que ya son el peor arranque del club en la historia de la competición. Suerte que el triunfo en la novedosa SuperCup ya haya asegurado un título y esté amortiguando los tropiezos recientes. Pese a las derrotas, el base ha demostrado su crecimiento. Tras la SuperCup, ha sido el máximo anotador y el jugador más valorado del conjunto madridista en tres de los cuatro encuentros. En la Euroliga es el segundo que más juega sólo por detrás de Edy Tavares (22:48 minutos), promedia 15,3 puntos, 6,0 asistencias y 22,7 créditos de valoración. Es el quinto mejor de la competición en esta última estadística. Este domingo, se plantará en Santiago para enfrentarse al recién ascendido Monbus Obradoiro (12.30 horas) después de haber firmado la mejor actuación de su carrera en la Euroliga. Este jueves, en la derrota ante el Hapoel Tel Aviv, hizo 26 puntos, cinco rebotes, siete asistencias y 40 de valoración. Frente al Unicaja, en la única jornada disputada en la Liga Endesa, acabó con 17 puntos, a uno de su mejor registro en ACB, y 23 de valoración, a tres de su tope. “La temporada es larga, pero lo importante es ser constante”, asegura un Maledon que ha trabajado mucho en el gimnasio este verano. Ha ganado tanto músculo como madurez en la pista. Su toma de decisiones parece mejor que hace un año mientras sigue siendo un cuchillo atravesando la zona rival y su facilidad para forzar tiros libres es oxígeno para los momentos de atasco. Su lunar, el triple. Si fuera más fiable, quizás no habría dejado la NBA.

articles.title: Fever's Kelsey Mitchell Says She'll Be 'Selfish' with Decision in 2026 WNBA Free Agency
articles.summary: Indiana Fever guard Kelsey Mitchell is prioritizing herself as she prepares to hit free agency.
articles.body:
Indiana Fever guard Kelsey Mitchell is prioritizing herself as she prepares to hit free agency.

"I have to be selfish," Mitchell said Saturday, per ESPN's Kareem Copeland . "I think that's where I am in my career ... what I probably need and what's probably best for me. So I have to be selfish in that room.

"But I think, ultimately, being on the Fever and being a part of an organization that does come with a lot of ups and downs, what factors in and what is important for me is, obviously, having a good chemistry on and off the floor. I've only been with one team my entire career, so it's all kind of like figuring this out. It's hard, man."

Indiana's 2026 season came to an end after it was eliminated by the Las Vegas Aces in the first round of the playoffs on Thursday night.

The Fever are now preparing to navigate through the offseason, with Mitchell set to become a free agent.

She's spent all nine years of her career as a member of the organization after Indiana selected her with the No. 2 overall pick in the 2018 WNBA draft. Mitchell has blossomed into a top offensive option for the Fever, earning All-Star nods in each of her past four seasons.

In 2026, the 30-year-old ranked No. 2 in the league with her scoring average of 24.7 points per game. She also recorded 2.8 assists, 1.7 rebounds and 1.0 steals on a nightly basis while shooting a career-high 50.9 percent from the field and 45.0 percent from three-point territory.

The Fever owned a plus-8.7 net rating with Mitchell on the court during the regular season compared to a minus-0.1 net rating with her off the floor (via WNBA.com ).

As Indiana looks to build around its young duo of Caitlin Clark and Aliyah Boston in order to contend for a fourth consecutive playoff berth in 2027, the future of Mitchell is something to monitor.

Nikola Jokić and his Denver Nuggets teammates were on the sidelines for Colorado's matchup against Texas Tech on Saturday.

Colorado head coach Deion Sanders met with the Nuggets and gave a speech to the team this past week as Denver opened its training camp. The Nuggets are holding their training camp at the Buffaloes' basketball facilities.

As for the football game, Colorado (2-2) had a tough matchup on its hands against No. 12 Texas Tech (4-0). The Buffs were hoping to avoid a third straight loss this season.

articles.title: Giannis Makes Heat Preseason Debut After Bucks Trade, Final Box Score Stats & Highlights
articles.summary: Giannis Antetokounmpo made his preseason debut for the Miami Heat on Saturday night.
articles.body:
Giannis Antetokounmpo made his preseason debut for the Miami Heat on Saturday night.

Antetokounmpo played 14 minutes in the first half of Miami's clash with the Toronto Raptors in Québec City after the Heat acquired him in a blockbuster trade with the Milwaukee Bucks on June 22.

Here's a closer look at how he fared through two quarters.

Antetokounmpo didn't appear to have any issue building chemistry with his new teammates, as he routinely kicked the ball out to open shooters after drawing extra defensive attention inside the arc.

His seven assists came against just two turnovers.

Antetokounmpo showcased his efficient scoring ability around the rim while also expanding his range, connecting on a one-legged fadeaway.

The Heat are coming off a 2025-26 campaign in which they missed the playoffs with a 43-39 record, but are looking to climb up the Eastern Conference standings with the two-time MVP in the mix.

Antetokounmpo appeared in 36 contests last season, averaging 27.6 points, 9.8 rebounds, 5.4 assists and 0.9 steals per game while shooting 62.4 percent from the field and 33.3 percent from three-point territory.

The Heat will open the 2026-27 regular season against the Minnesota Timberwolves on Oct. 21.

articles.title: Giannis Antetokounmpo posts 9 points, 7 assists in first Heat appearance, rests second half
articles.summary: Antetokounmpo rested in the second half, along with the other Miami starters.
articles.body:
The Miami Heat took on the Toronto Raptors in Québec City on Saturday night. While it marked the start of NBA preseason, it also marked star forward Giannis Antetokounmpo's first game appearance with his new team.

He played only the first half of Miami's 129-105 preseason blowout win, but that limited action was enough to affect the game and show how the Heat could use him on offense this season.

Antetokounmpo didn't score Miami's first points. Andrew Wiggins got the honor, nailing a 3 off a pass from Antetokounmpo. This became a common play for the Heat: the star forward barrels down the lane, then kicks out to the arc for a teammate to hit a 3.

The forward scored his first points with Miami on a layup early in the first quarter, and converted the and-one.

New team? Same fadeaway. Antetokounmpo made sure to pack his smooth jumper on the road trip.

The Miami forward finished the game with 9 points, 4 rebounds and 7 assists. Antetokounmpo shot a perfect 3-for-3 from the field but didn't attempt a 3-pointer. He also went 3-for-4 from the charity stripe.

The forward played 14 minutes in the first half and nearly had a double-double. With Miami up 20 through the first two quarters, the Heat rested their starters for the second half.

Antetokounmpo seemed to debut a new pre-game ritual. It will be interesting to see if he continues this in Miami or during the regular season. It is similar to the sprint that Russell Westbrook used to do down the court ahead of the action, with "The Greek Freak's" added flair.

Antetokounmpo finally got the trade he wanted this past summer as the Milwaukee Bucks sent him and Bobby Portis to Miami for Tyler Herro, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakučionis and five draft picks.

Saturday night's win over Toronto was the first of five preseason games the Heat will play. Miami will face the New Orleans Pelicans, Minnesota Timberwolves, Brooklyn Nets and Orlando Magic before beginning the regular season at home against Minnesota on Wednesday, Oct. 21.

articles.title: NBA trade rumor: Lakers could add 6-foot-6 Luka Doncic ex-teammate and Clippers forward as final roster piece
articles.summary: The Lakers overhauled their roster this summer, and one starting spot still looks unfinished.
articles.body: The Lakers overhauled their roster this summer, and one starting spot still looks unfinished. Walker Kessler and Quentin Grimes arrived, while LeBron James, Marcus Smart and Deandre Ayton left. Lakers need perimeter defense, secondary rim protection and enough offense to hold up. No one on the roster fits it as a proven power forward, and that probably doesn't change before opening night.Derrick Jones Jr. keeps coming up as the fix. The 6-foot-6 Clippers forward, 29, played one season beside Luka Doncic in Dallas, and a Clippers roster stripped of five first-round picks might listen. Reports published October 3 put him forward as an option. Nothing is agreed, and every idea here is speculation, not word from either front office.CategoryDetailsPlayerDerrick Jones Jr. (forward, 6-foot-6, 29)Current TeamLos Angeles ClippersRumored TeamLos Angeles LakersContract StatusFinal year; extension not expectedTrade LikelihoodSpeculative; Clippers' asking price unclearLatest Insider UpdateOct. 3: Lakers-Clippers deal proposed; asking price unclearPotential ReturnLaRavia, and three second-round picks to the Clippers (hypothetical)Why are the Lakers targeting Derrick Jones Jr.?Los Angeles has two in-house candidates in newcomers Ziaire Williams and Sandro Mamukelashvili, and either could claim the starting power forward job. Right now, it is fair to say that the newcomer duo is a backup option or a trade asset. Jones would upgrade any in-house option as a proven, veteran two-way contributor. His strength, agility and verticality suit a defender beside Doncic, who can feed him enough quality shots to stay viable on offense.What insiders are saying about the trade?As the summer roster changes happened, it looks like the Lakers are reaching the end of perfecting their team. Still, there are some gaps. "The Lakers need a forward and the Los Angeles Clippers need some draft capital, which makes these two teams the perfect trading partners," Fansided’s Mat Issa wrote. "This one would be another reunion for Dončić from his Finals run with the Dallas Mavericks. Here, the Lakers would trade LaRavia, Dalton Knecht and three second-round picks to get Derrick Jones Jr."Derrick Jones Jr.'s expiring deal and the Clippers' five lost first-roundersJones is in the final year of his contract and is not expected to get an extension. The league docked the Clippers five first-round picks, and the forward is believed to be among the veterans on their trade block. Moving him before the deadline would return something, while waiting risks losing him for nothing. Los Angeles could also hang back and wait for Jones to test free agency next summer. The Clippers' asking price is unclear.P.J. Washington in Dallas and Herbert Jones in New Orleans are other names on the radar, and Washington looks like the surer option.Doncic, Austin Reaves, Walker Kessler and Quentin Grimes already project as four starters, with one spot open. The clock runs in two directions. Los Angeles will judge Williams and Mamukelashvili over roughly two months, and the Clippers face the trade deadline with an expiring contract. If neither Laker claims the spot, the calls start. If the Clippers sit still, Jones may walk next summer with no return.
